Samanid page: Ismail Samani in 893 'invaded the territories of the Karluk Turks, taking Talas'; Kara-Khanid page: 'In the late 9th century, the Samanids marched into the steppes and captured Taraz, one of the headquarters of the Karluk khagan'. The shape has no Kashgar (its south edge is 41.0 N); Kashgar is added by the 934 gain ('converted to Islam in 934 and then captured Kashgar'), so this correction does not draw it for 896-933 (fixed after review: an earlier version added Kashgar to the whole span).

960-999: no change in the cells. Cliopatria's 960 shape plus Kashgar, which the Khanate holds from the 934 gain (ledger) except for Khotan's brief hold in 970 (Khotan page); the shape itself, as in 896-959, has no Kashgar, so the union is needed for 960 on.

1000-1009, 0.92 M km2: +1,706 cells in Transoxiana and Ferghana (62.6-76.2 E). Kara-Khanid page: 'by 999 Ali's son Nasr had taken Chach, Samarkand, and Bukhara'; Samanid page: 'In 999, Nasr b. Ali ... returned and took possession of Bukhara' and 'the Oxus River thus became the boundary between the two rival empires'. The shape fits (Oxus on the south).

Cliopatria's year is four years late and its shape reaches Korla (86.5 E), further east than the page says.
1040-1045: +5 cells on the Syr Darya and -1; no change. The page has the Khanate split 'in the 1040s' (1041: Muhammad 'Ayn ad-Dawlah in the west); Cliopatria's Eastern and Western rows begin in 1046.

region.text: Zhetysu, the Karluk country with Balasagun

ledger.note: 840: the Karluk khagan founds the Kara-Khanid Khanate. Infobox 'Established: 840'; ruler list 'Bilge Kul Qadir Khan (840-893)'; Karluk Yabghu page: after the Kyrgyz destroyed the Uyghur Khaganate in 840 the yabghu 'declared himself khagan as Bilge Kul Qadir Khan'.

region.text: Talas and Taraz and the lands east of them, up to eastern Fergana

ledger.note: 893: the Samanids take Talas. 'invaded the territories of the Karluk Turks, taking Talas and converting the Nestorian church there into a mosque' (893); Kara-Khanid page: they 'captured Taraz, one of the headquarters of the Karluk khagan'. The region is Cliopatria's 351-cell step of 896; the page names the town.

934: Satuq Bughra Khan takes Kashgar. 'converted to Islam in 934 and then captured Kashgar' (the page also gives 932 for the conversion and 960 for a mass conversion). The page does not say who held Kashgar.
970: Khotan takes Kashgar. 'Khotan briefly took Kashgar from the Kara-Khanids in 970.'

971: Kashgar back with the Kara-Khanids (bridging). The page says only 'briefly' and dates no return; 971 is the next dated Khotan entry (a letter to the Chinese emperor), and Khotan is not recorded holding Kashgar afterwards.

region.text: Isfijab, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand and Bukhara

ledger.note: 990: Hasan Bughra Khan invades the Samanids. 'Between 990 and 992, Hasan took Isfijab, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand, and the Samanid capital Bukhara'; Samanid page: Harun 'captured Bukhara' in 992 and died, and 'the Samanids returned to Bukhara'.

region.text: Chach, Samarkand, Bukhara and Ferghana: Transoxiana to the Oxus

ledger.note: 999: Nasr takes Bukhara and ends the Samanids. 'by 999 Ali's son Nasr had taken Chach, Samarkand, and Bukhara'; 'the Ilig occupied Bukhara definitively in 999'; the Oxus became the boundary with the Ghaznavids, who took Khorasan (Samanid page). Cliopatria's step is 1000.

region.text: Isfijab, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand and Bukhara

ledger.note: 999: the contest ends with the Samanid fall. 'In 999, Nasr b. Ali ... took possession of Bukhara, meeting little resistance'; Isma'il Muntasir's last attempt to restore the Samanids ended in 1005.

region.text: Khotan and the western Tarim Basin, 'which includes Khotan and Kashgar'

ledger.note: 1006: Yusuf Qadir Khan of Kashgar conquers Khotan. 'In 1006, Yusuf Qadir Khan of Kashgar conquered the Kingdom of Khotan, ending Khotan's existence as an independent state.' Cliopatria's shape (which also reaches Korla) steps in 1010.

region.text: the Eastern Khanate, 'capital at Balasaghun and later Kashgar' (the Zhetysu and Tarim Basin part of the Khanate; Cliopatria's Eastern row of 1046)

ledger.note: 1045: the Khanate divides into an Eastern and a Western Khanate. 'The Khanate split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s'; 1041: Muhammad 'Ayn ad-Dawlah takes the west, Ibrahim Tamghach Khan c. 1040-1068; the year 1045 is the last year of Cliopatria's row (confidence 1). fx-35 (1 Nov 2026): region narrowed from the whole 1045 Khanate (4,387 cells) to the Eastern Khanate (Cliopatria's Eastern Kara-Khanids shape of 1046, 3,298 cells, 3,296 of them inside the 1045 shape): the split handed the 1,090 Western cells to the Eastern state too and the Western Khanate's founding in 1046 then met them as a conflict. The Western part (Cliopatria's Western Karakhanid Khanate of 1046, 1,090 cells, Samarkand and Transoxiana; the two rows share no cell) goes to western-karakhanid-khanate at the dissolve below (identity.successors[1]). Kara-Khanid Khanate page: 'The Khanate split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s'; 'The Eastern Khanate had its capital at Balasaghun and later Kashgar'; 'The Fergana-Zhetysu areas became the border between the two states and were frequently contested.'

1045: the unified Khanate ends. The Western Khanate (capital Samarkand) and the Eastern (Balasagun, later Kashgar) share a border in the Fergana-Zhetysu areas; Cliopatria's Eastern and Western rows begin in 1046.

wars.name: Samanid conquest of Talas
wars.outcome: Ismail Samani took Talas and Taraz from the Karluks and converted the Nestorian church into a mosque.

wars.name: Khotan-Kara-Khanid wars
wars.outcome: Khotan briefly took Kashgar in 970; in 1006 Yusuf Qadir Khan of Kashgar conquered Khotan and ended the kingdom.
wars.note: The Khotan page has no dated clash between 971 and 1006.

wars.name: Karakhanid-Samanid wars

zones.text: Isfijab, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand and Bukhara

wars.outcome: Hasan Bughra Khan took Isfijab, Ferghana, Samarkand and Bukhara in 990-992 (Harun took Bukhara in 992 and the Samanids returned); Nasr took Chach, Samarkand and Bukhara by 999 and the Samanids ended; the Oxus became the Ghaznavid-Kara-Khanid boundary.

wars.name: Seljuk-Kara-Khanid conflict
wars.outcome: After the Seljuk victory over the Ghaznavids at Dandanaqan (1040) 'Conflict with the Karakhanids broke out, but the Karakhanids were able to withstand attacks by the Seljuks initially'; no land changed hands.

certainty.note: Frontiers between steppe, oasis and mountain are approximate; the Oxus frontier with the Ghaznavids from 999 ('The Oxus River thus became the boundary between the two rival empires') is the one firm line.

notes:
Pages opened: Kara-Khanid Khanate (three queries, the third on the repair pass), Samanid Empire, Kingdom of Khotan, Karluk Yabghu and Karluks (5 distinct pages, budget 5).
One state or three: the Kara-Khanid page lists the Khanate as one state from 840 that 'split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s'; Wikidata Q494354 is shared by Cliopatria's Kara-Khanids (850-1045), Eastern Kara-Khanids (1046-1138) and Western Karakhanid Khanate (1046-1084). This dossier covers the unified Khanate (the first row only, 840-1045); after the split the Eastern and Western Khanates are different states with different capitals (Balasagun/Kashgar and Samarkand), written by other batches (eastern-kara-khanids, western-karakhanid-khanate in ia-01), and the 1045 split/dissolve events hand the land to them. The split year is not on the page ('the 1040s'); 1045 is Cliopatria's.
Start moved from Cliopatria's 850 to 840 (infobox) with a new keyframe; the Qarlugs row 840-849 is the same land (see qarlugs notes: the two rows are one Karluk polity on the Karluk Yabghu page).
Tarim Basin 850-933: Cliopatria draws 880 Tarim cells (Kashgar and the west) in the Kara-Khanid shape from 850 and hands them to its Khotan row in 888; the pages put the Kara-Khanid capture of Kashgar in 934 and the Khotan independence in 851, so the shapes 850-886 are adjusted to drop the Tarim and a gain of Kashgar is added at 934 (counterpart nobody: the page does not say who held it). The Khotan dossier carries the Tarim from 851. The 1010 step is the page's 1006 conquest of Khotan.
No area is on the Kara-Khanid page, so the infobox comparison is not possible; the Samanid page gives 2.85 M km2 for 928, not comparable. Rulers: on the repair pass the page's ruler list was read; its sequential entries 840-1017 are in identity.rulers (the list mixes the later Eastern and Western lines, so 958-970 and 1018-1045 have no ruler).
Missing: 1017-1018 (the page: 'the Karakhanids repelled an attack by a large mass of nomadic Turkic tribes'), the Ghaznavid wars (no Mahmud dates on the page), the Qocho and Khitan frontiers (the page gives no dates), Uzgen as a capital (undated). Gazetteer: Balasagun, Kashgar, Taraz exist; the Tarim 'Kashgar' radius is a place radius.
Repair pass (review ia-01-f): keyframe 896-959 no longer adds Kashgar (the 934 ledger gain and the 960 keyframe carry it). Re-read of the Kara-Khanid page: it is silent on who held Kashgar before 934 (only 'of the old Shule Kingdom'; the Yagma lived 'south and east of the Karluks'), so the 934 gain keeps counterpart 'nobody'; silent on Khotan's 970 seizure of Kashgar and on its return (the Khotan page is the only source, 971 stays a confidence-1 bridge); silent on a 1006 Khorasan invasion and a 1008 Balkh defeat (not added: the Ghaznavids page was not opened, the 5-page budget being spent). It dates 'Around 1017-1018' a partition of the former Samanid lands along the Oxus between Ilig Khan and Mahmud of Ghazni (no ledger event type fits a treaty; the Oxus frontier is in the certainty note). The split is 'in the 1040s', with 1041 only as Muhammad 'Ayn ad-Dawlah's accession in the west; 1045 stays Cliopatria's year at confidence 1. Capitals: infobox 'Balasagun (942-1130); Kashgar (1130-1211); Samarkand (1040-1212)' and Uzgen undated in the body, so no change. I disagree with no finding of the review; the Ghaznavid frontier events and the pre-934 holder of Kashgar stay open (see the report's gaps).
